S.TRANSL: Once upon a time, there was a girl orphan.
She didn't have her parents when she was still a little child.
She had no one to support her, and she was lonely each day.

S.FORM: nakai ma-manəŋ=pa si Ɂuna ŋuain tanasa tu-Ɂuna.
S.PHON: nakai mamanəŋpa ʂi ʔuna ŋuain tanasa tuʔuna
S.FORM: nakai mamanengpa si 'una nguain tanasa tu'una.
S.PHON: nakai mamaneŋpa ʂi ʔuna ŋuain tanasa tuʔuna
S.TRANSL: Fortunately, she had a house to live in.
In that way, she had to look for food by herself.
She grew up in that way.

S.FORM: Ɂuna u-cani taniarə, ni-k<əm>aənə=cu ku-caɁan ia, surumu ma-taməməŋ, nakai Ɂuna tiɁiŋ taniarə, ara-pa-piniŋ tia=a-pa-sanuŋu tikuru.
S.PHON: ʔuna uʦani taniarə nikəmaənəʦu kuʦaʔan ia surumu mataməməŋ nakai ʔuna tiʔiŋ taniarə arapapiniŋ tiaapasanuŋu tikuru
S.FORM: 'una ucani taniare, nik<em>aenecu kuca'an ia, surumu matamemeng, nakai 'una ti'ing taniare, arapapining tiaapasanungu tikuru.
S.PHON: ʔuna uʦani tania[r|ɾ]e nikemaeneʦu kuʦaʔan ia su[r|ɾ]umu matamemeŋ nakai ʔuna tiʔiŋ tania[r|ɾ]e a[r|ɾ]apapiniŋ tiaapasanuŋu tiku[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: On a certain day, when she had eaten lunch, suddenly, it drizzled, but there was a little sunshine, as she went out to gather clothes.

S.FORM: tara-kusa sipar-a naini sua ma-niŋcau cəɁəra-ənə.
S.PHON: tarakusa ʂipara naini sua maniŋʦau ʦəʔəraənə
S.FORM: tarakusa sipara naini sua maningcau ce'eraene.
S.PHON: ta[r|ɾ]akusa ʂipa[r|ɾ]a naini sua maniŋʦau ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]aene
S.TRANSL: The girl was facing the other side (of the river), something looked very pretty.
She looked at it carefully, and it turned out to be a rainbow, really pretty.
Ever since then she loved to see the rainbow.

S.FORM: aranai=cu mia-sua nuu ara-pa-piniŋ-in valanvana ia, mu-kusa-ən=kiai ma-caaɁə ramisi varanvana.
S.PHON: aranaiʦu miasua nuu arapapiniŋin vaɾanvana ia mukusaənkiai maʦaaʔə ramiʂi varanvana
S.FORM: aranaicu miasua nuu arapapiningin varanvana ia, mukusaenkiai macaa'e ramisi varanvana.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anaiʦu miasua nuu a[r|ɾ]apapiniŋin va[r|ɾ]anvana ia mukusaenkiai maʦaaʔe [r|ɾ]amiʂi va[r|ɾ]anvana
S.TRANSL: Since then when the rainbow appeared, she went to catch the end of the rainbow.
In that way, she went to catch the end of the rainbow many times.
Carelessly, her hand touched a hundred pacer (type of snake).

S.FORM: nakai sua vunai ia, a-caa=cu pu-aiɁi na Ɂaravaŋ-in.
S.PHON: nakai sua vunai ia aʦaaʦu puaiʔi na ʔaravaŋin
S.FORM: nakai sua vunai ia, acaacu puai'i na 'aravangin.
S.PHON: nakai sua vunai ia aʦaaʦu puaiʔi na ʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋin
S.TRANSL: But the snake returned to the cave.
The girl was frightened.
In that way she returned to her house.
Formerly the rainbow still appeared.
She did not go to the base of the rainbow any more.

S.FORM: aranai=cu mia-sua mu-caaca. na nəmər-a tia=kirimi ranəŋə kaalu.
S.PHON: aranaiʦu miasua muʦaaʦa na nəməra tiakirimi ranəŋə kaaɾu
S.FORM: aranaicu miasua mucaaca. na nemera tiakirimi ranenge kaaru.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anaiʦu miasua muʦaaʦa na neme[r|ɾ]a tiaki[r|ɾ]imi [r|ɾ]aneŋe kaa[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: Ever since then she walked to the jungle to look for tree leaves.

S.FORM: Ɂuna ma-sinaŋ, Ɂuna ta-vacuku, Ɂuna ta-navikarə, Ɂuna ta-Ɂələm, Ɂuna ta-punia, Ɂuna ɁulaɁula, ma-sinaŋ, ɁulaɁula, ta-navikarə, u-pitu tapasə ni-alamə=kiai.
S.PHON: ʔuna maʂinaŋ ʔuna tavaʦuku ʔuna tanavikarə ʔuna taʔəɾəm ʔuna tapunia ʔuna ʔuɾaʔuɾa maʂinaŋ ʔuɾaʔuɾa tanavikarə upitu tapasə niaɾaməkiai
S.FORM: 'una masinang, 'una tavacuku, 'una tanavikare, 'una ta'erem, 'una tapunia, 'una 'ura'ura, masinang, 'ura'ura, tanavikare, upitu tapase niaramekiai.
S.PHON: ʔuna maʂinaŋ ʔuna tavaʦuku ʔuna tanavika[r|ɾ]e ʔuna taʔe[r|ɾ]em ʔuna tapunia ʔuna ʔu[r|ɾ]aʔu[r|ɾ]a maʂinaŋ ʔu[r|ɾ]aʔu[r|ɾ]a tanavika[r|ɾ]e upitu tapase nia[r|ɾ]amekiai
S.TRANSL: They were in red, green, yellow, black, white, pink, and light yellow; altogether she picked up seven types of color.

S.FORM: paira makasua mu-kusa nəmər-a m-alamə u-pitu tapasə.
S.PHON: paira makasua mukusa nəməra maɾamə upitu tapasə
S.FORM: paira makasua mukusa nemera marame upitu tapase.
S.PHON: pai[r|ɾ]a makasua mukusa neme[r|ɾ]a ma[r|ɾ]ame upitu tapase
S.TRANSL: She often went to the jungle to pick up tree leaves in seven types of color.

S.FORM: mia i-tumulu=cu ranəŋə ni-alam-a, ala-ənə=kiai pa-sanəli pakaɁ-in=kiai valanvana tamna tapasə.
S.PHON: mia itumuɾuʦu ranəŋə niaɾama aɾaənəkiai pasanəɾi pakaʔinkiai vaɾanvana tamna tapasə
S.FORM: mia itumurucu ranenge niarama, araenekiai pasaneri paka'inkiai varanvana tamna tapase.
S.PHON: mia itumu[r|ɾ]uʦu [r|ɾ]aneŋe nia[r|ɾ]ama a[r|ɾ]aenekiai pasane[r|ɾ]i pakaʔinkiai va[r|ɾ]anvana tamna tapase
S.TRANSL: When she picked up many leaves, she spread them out to show the different colors of the rainbow.
She worked in that manner each day.

S.FORM: Ɂuna u-cani taniarə ni-ara-naturu sua maanu nanakə.
S.PHON: ʔuna uʦani taniarə niaranaturu sua maanu nanakə
S.FORM: 'una ucani taniare niaranaturu sua maanu nanake.
S.PHON: ʔuna uʦani tania[r|ɾ]e nia[r|ɾ]anatu[r|ɾ]u sua maanu nanake
S.TRANSL: On a certain day, the girl became dumb.

S.FORM: paira ma-ruka, ma-pinipiŋ ŋuain tamna kin-cau-a si i-tumulu=cu taniarə kaɁan pu-aiɁi tanasa.
S.PHON: paira maruka mapinipiŋ ŋuain tamna kinʦaua ʂi itumuɾuʦu taniarə kaʔan puaiʔi tanasa
S.FORM: paira maruka, mapiniping nguain tamna kincaua si itumurucu taniare ka'an puai'i tanasa.
S.PHON: pai[r|ɾ]a ma[r|ɾ]uka mapinipiŋ ŋuain tamna kinʦaua ʂi itumu[r|ɾ]uʦu tania[r|ɾ]e kaʔan puaiʔi tanasa
S.TRANSL: She often got lost, and her relatives were nervous because she did not return home for many days.
Her relatives could not find her.
In that way the girl got lost for a long time.
